claim: A specialist-market model's inspected introduction shows superior counterparty information can generate a positive bid-ask spread even under a risk-neutral specialist earning zero expected transaction profit, and that binding inventory constraints can force departure from that zero-profit pricing.
locator: Author-hosted reprint PDF pp. 1-3; abstract and opening Section 1
limitations: Only the abstract and opening Section 1 were inspected, not the formal model or proofs; a stock specialist-market analogy, not direct evidence for any prediction venue; the chapter's fill-conditioned mixture derivation is independently constructed.

claim: A continuous-auction model describes an equilibrium with one risk-neutral insider, noise traders and competitive risk-neutral market makers in which, in the continuous-trading limit, prices follow a Brownian process with constant depth and eventual full information incorporation.
limitations: Only the complete abstract was inspected, not the full article or proofs; an equilibrium conclusion under a specified model, not an empirical law of event-market prices.

claim: An inventory-aware limit-order-book market-making model builds a finite-horizon reservation-price/quote-skew rule on a driftless arithmetic Brownian mid-price, exponential terminal-wealth utility and distance-decaying Poisson arrivals, with its simple quoted bid/ask expressions (equations 29-30) stated as an approximation and its reported performance from numerical simulations marked to the terminal midpoint.
limitations: Main text and cited equations were inspected, not the Appendix in full; terminal midpoint valuation is not an executed liquidation or a binary contractual settlement. A binary payout does not require a price jump at the administrative settlement instant.

locator: The gambler with a private wire, pp. 918-920; The general case, pp. 920-922; track take, pp. 923-925; Conclusion, pp. 925-926
